content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# RN legacy same-PR platforms

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native legacy bridge work must close both iOS and Android sides in the same PR, because half-bridging one platform leaves the other as a half-coverage hop that makes agents read. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 2 states both iOS and Android sides must close in the same PR and explains the half-bridge failure mode.

# Rationale: Lua value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: accepted

Corrected bootstrap edge shape: the validation invariant is a constraint and should constrain the proposed decision rather than be attached as an isMotivatedBy target.

# RN legacy bridge resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves React Native legacy JS `NativeModules.X.fn(...)` calls to Objective-C `RCT_EXPORT_METHOD` / `RCT_REMAP_METHOD` and Java/Kotlin `@ReactMethod` implementations using module names from `RCT_EXPORT_MODULE` or `getName()`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks RN legacy bridge done, with AsyncStorage 8/8 precise and react-native-firebase 18 precise after blocking `RCTEventEmitter` built-ins.

# Native bridge dynamic frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph native-bridge coverage remains limited around nonliteral or generated bridge forms: Swift generics over ObjC protocols, Swift extensions on ObjC classes, React Native dynamic module keys, TurboModule native impl classes without legacy macros, Expo trailing-closure bodies, and Fabric event-handler props. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 lists these as hole-identified frontiers across Swift/ObjC, RN legacy, TurboModules, Expo Modules, and Fabric/Paper rows.

# Fabric view extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts React Native Fabric and legacy Paper view components from Codegen TS specs, `RCT_EXPORT_VIEW_PROPERTY`, and `@ReactProp`, then synthesizes component-to-native implementation links by RN naming conventions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Fabric/Paper views done and validates RNSegmentedControl, RNScreens, and RNSkia, including monorepo package detection for RNSkia.

content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# RN legacy same-PR platforms

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native legacy bridge work must close both iOS and Android sides in the same PR, because half-bridging one platform leaves the other as a half-coverage hop that makes agents read. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 2 states both iOS and Android sides must close in the same PR and explains the half-bridge failure mode.

# Phase one bridge gate

Lifecycle status: proposed

Phase 2 must not begin until Swift-Objective-C bridging passes the mixed iOS §5a validation bar on Charts, Realm-Cocoa, and Wikipedia-iOS. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 1 says to validate on the Charts/Realm/Wikipedia corpus before moving on and not proceed to Phase 2 until Phase 1 passes the §5a bar on all three repos.

# Native bridge validation corpus

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge work should be validated on real small, medium, and large mixed iOS and React Native repositories plus a narrower Expo corpus, each with canonical cross-bridge flows. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §5 lists candidate small/medium/large repos for mixed iOS and React Native, two Expo scopes, and says the implementation PR confirms choices after verifying each repo still builds an index cleanly.

# Per-channel native bridge resolvers

Lifecycle status: proposed

Each mixed iOS or React Native bridging mechanism should be modeled as its own dispatch channel with its own resolver or synthesizer, validation, and playbook matrix row. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §2 says each row is a separate dispatch channel in the playbook vocabulary, each gets its own resolver or synthesizer, validation, and §6 matrix row.

# Swift generic bridge misses

Lifecycle status: proposed

Swift-only generics over Objective-C protocols can be silently missed by the native bridge plan, while `@objc` Swift extensions on ObjC classes still follow the Phase 1 path. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 says Swift-only generics over ObjC protocols are not handled and silently missed, while `@objc` extension methods use the same Phase 1 path; this is acceptable and matches the Java/Kotlin generics frontier.

content.text:
Top 5 recorded entries:

# RN legacy same-PR platforms

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native legacy bridge work must close both iOS and Android sides in the same PR, because half-bridging one platform leaves the other as a half-coverage hop that makes agents read. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 2 states both iOS and Android sides must close in the same PR and explains the half-bridge failure mode.

# React Native bridge closure

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native bridge coverage must close JS-to-native and native-to-JS event flows across both legacy bridge and TurboModules, because mixed bridge styles otherwise create half-bridged apps. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §1 says JS-to-native and native-to-JS must both close on both legacy bridge and TurboModules, or apps that mix them will half-bridge.

# Native bridge validation corpus

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge work should be validated on real small, medium, and large mixed iOS and React Native repositories plus a narrower Expo corpus, each with canonical cross-bridge flows. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §5 lists candidate small/medium/large repos for mixed iOS and React Native, two Expo scopes, and says the implementation PR confirms choices after verifying each repo still builds an index cleanly.

# Mixed iOS bridge closure

Lifecycle status: proposed

Mixed iOS bridge coverage must close both Swift-to-Objective-C and Objective-C-to-Swift directions, including methods, properties, initializers, and protocols, before measuring or shipping the flow. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §1 says for mixed iOS both directions and all bridged kinds must close before measuring.

# No JVM extractor redesign

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native bridge work should use the Kotlin and Java extraction quality already available and only allow tiny refinements for missing `@ReactMethod` literal names, not a redesign of JVM extraction. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 marks Android Kotlin/Java extraction quality out of scope and narrows allowable work to tiny extractor refinement for annotation literal names.

CodeGraph resolves React Native legacy JS `NativeModules.X.fn(...)` calls to Objective-C `RCT_EXPORT_METHOD` / `RCT_REMAP_METHOD` and Java/Kotlin `@ReactMethod` implementations using module names from `RCT_EXPORT_MODULE` or `getName()`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks RN legacy bridge done, with AsyncStorage 8/8 precise and react-native-firebase 18 precise after blocking `RCTEventEmitter` built-ins.

# Native bridge dynamic frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph native-bridge coverage remains limited around nonliteral or generated bridge forms: Swift generics over ObjC protocols, Swift extensions on ObjC classes, React Native dynamic module keys, TurboModule native impl classes without legacy macros, Expo trailing-closure bodies, and Fabric event-handler props. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 lists these as hole-identified frontiers across Swift/ObjC, RN legacy, TurboModules, Expo Modules, and Fabric/Paper rows.

# Fabric view extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts React Native Fabric and legacy Paper view components from Codegen TS specs, `RCT_EXPORT_VIEW_PROPERTY`, and `@ReactProp`, then synthesizes component-to-native implementation links by RN naming conventions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Fabric/Paper views done and validates RNSegmentedControl, RNScreens, and RNSkia, including monorepo package detection for RNSkia.

# RN event channel synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph synthesizes React Native native-to-JS event edges by matching native `sendEventWithName`, Swift `sendEvent(withName:)`, and JVM `.emit()` literal event names to JS `addListener` handlers, with a subscribe-wrapper fallback for library APIs. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks `rn-event-channel` done, using the same `EVENT_FANOUT_CAP=6` and validating RNFirebase push-notification and RNGeolocation location-event flows.

item.text:
The recorded requirements most directly tied to `RN legacy same-PR platforms` are:

- `React Native bridge closure` - React Native bridge coverage must close JS-to-native and native-to-JS flows across both legacy bridge and TurboModules, so mixed bridge styles do not leave half-bridged apps.
- `RN native implementation sibling links` - the iOS and Android implementations of the same JS-visible React Native or Expo method should be linked to each other, so a call reaching one platform is understood as reaching the other.

If you want, I can also trace which architectural decision entry this constraint was attached to in the memory graph.
